scope: Offline analysis of the previously verified complete snapshot; authorization is not a device-execution result
implementation_state: Existing uncommitted RAW-v1 sources; no new build, CI, firmware or kernel selection

analysis.method: Unpack little-endian signature/next/size; validate full ring; rotate raw[12:] at next-write offset 0x3cbd2. Count ASCII lines and case-insensitive category matches without exposing raw text or identifiers.
analysis.keymaster_interpretation: 837 complete repeated init messages report that hwservicemanager's interface_start request cannot find the keymaster service; one older message is truncated at the full-ring boundary. This is Android Recovery/fastbootd context, not ArmCpu or ArmDTPlatform failure.
analysis.display_error_labels: 12 Android DRM ERROR-labelled lines concern panel preparation/backlight updates; severity labels alone do not establish a display failure or native XNU defect.
analysis.tail: Android records a power-control reboot request from fastbootd, shutdown handling, storage-cache synchronization and restart. This is compatible with the separately recorded deployment reboot, but the text is not an independently authenticated operation identifier or a native reset-retention test.
analysis.conclusion: The exported full ring is dominated by pre-native Android console traffic. It explains the full/nonlinear-header admission obstacle; it is not evidence of a native kernel crash or progress. Native launch remains unperformed in the observed workflow.

limits: A full ring has already overwritten older history. Missing text markers cannot prove a stage never ran outside this retained snapshot.
No claim of exclusive RAM ownership, native permanent mapping, DMA exclusion, crash recovery or reset retention follows from these Android bytes.
Init must compare the live candidate and entire snapshot SHA before receipt input and two separate confirmations; any mismatch requires a separate read-only export, not a forced write.
An Init success would establish an initialization receipt only, not an ARM or a running XNU session.
